title: Single pricing authority on config/pricing.yaml; fail-closed catalog; unknown-model raise-with-cap/UNPRICED; coverage gate
findings_partially_addressed: F-13 (coverage-gate half only; cap-enforcement/atomicity half is TP-RTE-TRUTH-R2-003)

problem_summary.F-10_fail_open_catalog_collapse: lib/spend_ledger.py kept its own hardcoded $0.15/$0.60 MODEL_COST_RATES baseline, overwritten by benchmarking.pricing.catalog when importable, and silently KEPT (fail-open) whenever that import or catalog load failed for ANY reason (bare except Exception -> logger.warning -> return {}). Every model then priced at the $0.15/$0.60 baseline while get_model_cost_rate still reported match_type='exact', unknown_model=False -- a 33-50x under-price presented with full confidence.
problem_summary.F-11_two_authorities_disagree: E2 (SpendLedger, powers --print-cost-preview and the pre-dispatch preventive check) priced usage via catalog rates x service_tier/batch/cache multipliers. E3 (SpendTrackerState/estimate_usage_cost_usd, the authoritative post-response abort tracker) priced the SAME usage flat against pricing.yaml with zero multipliers. On flex-tier profiles (OpenAI flex = 0.5x) this is exactly 2x divergence: a run projected to fit the cap under E2 could be E3-aborted at roughly half the expected work, and vice versa. Both trackers ran simultaneously and both could independently abort.

design_summary.single_authority: extractor/costing.py is now the ONLY pricing authority. load_pricing_registry(path) reads config/pricing.yaml directly and raises RuntimeError on any problem (missing file, bad YAML, missing/empty models map, malformed/negative row) -- no fallback branch, ever. resolve_model_rate() is the one candidate-matching lookup (moved verbatim from the old spend_ledger.py logic) used by both authorities. compute_optimized_cost() (the money math with service_tier/batch/cache multipliers) and estimate_usage_cost_usd() (Decimal accounting math, now accepting the SAME optional service_tier/is_batch/cached_input_tokens context) both live here too.
design_summary.spend_ledger_is_now_a_facade: lib/spend_ledger.py deleted MODEL_COST_RATES, _catalog_rates(), _fallback_cost_rate(), the benchmarking.pricing.catalog import, and all $0.15/$0.60-as-pricing-fallback logic (~330 lines net). get_model_cost_rate() is now a thin wrapper: extractor.costing.load_pricing_registry_cached(...) (raises, fail closed) -> extractor.costing.resolve_model_rate(...) -> decorate with pricing_surface_metadata. SpendLedger.price_usage/accumulate delegate compute_optimized_cost/make_projected_cost_check to extractor.costing (re-exported, not reimplemented).
design_summary.unknown_model_policy: SpendLedger.price_usage now checks self.record.global_max_cost_usd is not None (the exact field run_extraction_v5.py sets from cfg.max_cost_usd when constructing the ledger, i.e. 'a cost cap is active') immediately after resolving the rate. Unknown model + cap set -> raises RuntimeError (mirrors E3's existing 'Missing pricing for route' raise -- E2 now aligns with E3 instead of E3 aligning down to E2's old fail-open behavior). Unknown model + no cap -> unknown_model=True, pricing_status=UNPRICED_UNKNOWN, cost fields are exactly 0.0 (never a fabricated baseline or max-of-registry number). lib/prescan/cost_estimator.py's _get_pricing_rate got the same treatment: a catalog LOAD failure now propagates (fail closed) instead of being caught by a blanket except-and-substitute-0.15/0.60; an unknown MODEL is marked unpriced (0.0, unpriced=True flag surfaced in pricing_basis) instead of silently defaulting.
design_summary.cross_authority_math_parity: estimate_usage_cost_usd (E3) gained optional service_tier / is_batch / cached_input_tokens kwargs, applying the identical multiplier semantics as compute_optimized_cost (E2) via new Decimal-safe helpers (_decimal_tier_multiplier, _decimal_cached_rate) so a caller that supplies the same optimizer context to both gets the same number. record_request_cost (E3's production entrypoint) threads these through. NOTE (residual, documented below): the real dispatch call site in run_extraction_v5.py (enrich_request_meta, 13+ call sites) does not yet auto-derive service_tier/is_batch/cached_input_tokens from live response meta and pass them into record_request_cost -- that full-pipeline wiring was deliberately deferred (see Remaining Uncertainty) as out of the minimal-correct-change boundary for this packet; the unified formula itself is implemented, tested, and available for that follow-up wiring.
design_summary.coverage_gate: New tests/test_pricing_coverage_gate.py resolves every route reachable from every COST_PROFILES entry (cell_aliases + hardcoded ladder fallbacks) across ALL phases via the existing run_extraction_v5.collect_provider_routes (the same resolver initialize_spend_tracker's own missing-route check already uses at startup) and asserts each has a numeric priced row in config/pricing.yaml. Running this gate against the pre-fix pricing.yaml found 5 REAL gaps (see below); config/pricing.yaml was updated to close them. A self-check test proves the gate is not vacuous (it fails against a deliberately near-empty registry).

These are hardcoded fallback models in run_extraction_v5.py's ACTIVE_ROUTING_LADDERS (openrouter-resilient ladder) -- not present in promptsets/ (out of my edit scope), so read-only verification only.

golden_diff.explanation: The golden harness's cost-preview scenario exercises the HAPPY PATH: a normal, successful catalog load with a known model. F-10/F-11's defects only manifest (a) when the catalog fails to load at all, or (b) when comparing E2's preview/preventive numbers against E3's SEPARATE accounting run -- the golden harness only snapshots one code path's happy-path output, not a cross-authority comparison. Since config/pricing.yaml's rates for the golden's exercised models were already identical to the old catalog-derived MODEL_COST_RATES values in the success case, the happy-path preview number is unchanged. No golden was silently re-baselined; all 28 golden assertions passed against the pre-existing committed goldens with zero diff, confirmed by running with RTE_TRUTH_SLOW_GOLDENS=1 (the flag that includes the cost-preview golden, normally skipped for speed).

residual_risks_and_deferred_work: F-13's cap-enforcement/atomicity half (post_hoc one-call overshoot, cost_cap_mode decorative flag, spend-ledger atomic writes) is explicitly out of scope here -- owned by TP-RTE-TRUTH-R2-003 per CONSOLIDATED-FINDINGS.md.

The real dispatch call site (run_extraction_v5.py's enrich_request_meta, 13+ call sites feeding record_request_cost) does not yet auto-derive service_tier/is_batch/cached_input_tokens from live provider response meta and thread them into E3's accounting. The UNIFIED FORMULA is implemented and proven equal for identical context (this packet's core requirement); wiring that context through 13+ call sites in a 22k-line file was assessed as materially higher risk than the packet's minimal-correct-change mandate justified, given: (a) the base/no-optimizer-context case (the vast majority of calls, and the ONLY case reachable without a cap-set or exotic tier config) is already exactly unified by the single-authority fix, and (b) response_summary.usage's raw key-shape (prompt_tokens/completion_tokens vs input_tokens/output_tokens/cached_tokens) differs between what E2's normalizer and E3's reader currently expect, and resolving that ambiguity safely needs deeper tracing than this packet's time budget allowed. Recommend a focused follow-up packet.

The 5 newly-added pricing.yaml rows (openrouter/openai/gpt-5.2-chat, gpt-5.2-pro, gpt-5-pro, gpt-4.1-nano, gpt-4o-mini) are LOW/MEDIUM-confidence inferred rates pending live-page verification -- flagged explicitly via pricing_confidence + pricing_caveat, not silently presented as confirmed.

_pricing_preview_record in run_extraction_v5.py (a peripheral, non-authoritative retry-cost hotspot reporting helper used only when cfg.ledger is None, which is never true in a normal run) still references the legacy BASELINE_INPUT/OUTPUT_COST_PER_1M_USD constants for its fallback math.
